threats.name: reopening Integer, Module and the gate methods
threats.rationale: Ruby classes are open: any code in the process can redefine Integer#==, Integer.===, Module#===, Kernel methods or LogicGates.nand_gate, and the gates call each other by name at call time (gates.rb:435, :462, :498, :540). MITRE CWE-471 (modification of assumed-immutable data) is the nearest entry.

threats.name: the exception message carries a caller-chosen class name unescaped

Probed on MRI 3.4.10 (not a committed test): the message came back with the newline and the escape sequence intact. closed_by.detail: gates.rb:122-128 builds "an instance of #{name}" from the real class name (bound Module#name) truncated to 64 characters; the truncation does not remove newlines or escape sequences, and Module#set_temporary_name (Ruby 3.3+) lets a caller choose any non-constant string as an anonymous class's name.

threats.name: describing a huge Integer in an error message

threats.name: wrong number of arguments, trailing keywords and and_n/or_n identity
threats.rationale: Ruby raises ArgumentError for a wrong argument count, so a gate cannot silently ignore an extra argument. threats.name: combinational and sequential use a weaker, differently-typed bit check
threats.rationale: The 11 gates use Integer === with InvalidBitError, but the combinational and sequential blocks carry their own copy of the check: `value.is_a?(Integer)` raising TypeError for a non-Integer and ArgumentError for a bad value (combinational.rb:448-456, sequential.rb:71), and they interpolate `width.inspect` and `direction.inspect` of a caller value (sequential.rb:463, :467, :547).
